reference_opening.argument: This video is non-scam content because it presents an instructional Firefox workflow for opening Search settings and selecting a default engine such as Bing, DuckDuckGo, or Ecosia. The material describes browser configuration and testing a search choice rather than requesting payment, credentials, investment participation, or other financial action. Disclosed affiliate links are presented as ordinary promotional context and are not connected to a deceptive offer or the Firefox instructions.

citations.quote: How to Change Default Search Engine in Firefox - Bing, DuckDuckGo, Ecosia
The first thing we need to do to change the default search engine in Firefox is simply open the menu by selecting the 3 horizontal lines in the top right.
I'm gonna add Ecosia, which is a search engine that plants trees every time you use the search engine
Once it's installed all we need to do is go back to the Firefox options, and then in the drop down we'll find our new desired search engine and we can select it.

opening.argument: Judge the sequence, not just the Firefox settings screen. The presenter says Ecosia plants trees whenever it is used, then directs viewers to install its search plug-in and make it their default engine. That links an easy, recurring benefit to a concrete action: add the tool and route searches through it. The tutorial format does not erase that solicitation; it makes the action look like a routine browser preference.

citations.quote: Ecosia, which is a search engine that plants trees every time you use the search engine
I'm going to select the search plug-in and then just select Add to Firefox
Once you select the search engine, you're done. You don't have to save anything, it automatically saves

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense accurately describes the settings steps, but those steps are also how the viewer is steered toward the promoted engine. Its point about no payment or credentials does not address the benefit tied to using Ecosia: the presenter explicitly pairs tree planting with adding its plug-in. The disclosed affiliate links are separate; the concern here is the promised benefit attached to changing search behavior.

citations.quote: I'm gonna add Ecosia, which is a search engine that plants trees every time you use the search engine, so I'm going to select the search plug-in and then just select Add to Firefox

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The quoted tree-planting description is not a promise that the viewer will receive a reward or acquire an asset. The demonstrated action is choosing a search provider in Firefox, and the presenter tells viewers to find their own desired engine. Nothing cited establishes a claim flow, a payout, or a deceptive offer.

citations.quote: find your desired search engine
in the drop down we'll find our new desired search engine and we can select it

opening.argument: Several signals warrant a closer look together: the video sends viewers from Firefox settings to a search-tool installation, promotes a benefit from using the selected engine, and places outside promotional and paid links in the description. The links do not prove the search plug-in is fraudulent. They do, however, mean the judge should not treat the presence of genuine browser instructions as conclusive evidence that the benefit-led installation pitch is merely neutral instruction.

citations.quote: select Find More Search Engines at the bottom.
Ecosia, which is a search engine that plants trees every time you use the search engine
Disclaimer: Some of the links in this description are Amazon affiliate links.
HOW DO I DO IT? (Paid Links)

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense calls the affiliate material ordinary promotional context, and the disclosure supports that reading. But disclosure alone does not settle how to read the main video: it still moves from a claimed benefit to installing and selecting a search tool. Nor does showing authentic Firefox settings establish whether the benefit claim has been substantiated.

citations.quote: Some of the links in this description are Amazon affiliate links.
I'm gonna add Ecosia, which is a search engine that plants trees every time you use the search engine

true_side_reply.rebuttal: These signals are not evidence of a deceptive reward offer. The description identifies the affiliate links as paid links, while the search-tool steps are part of changing Firefox's default search engine. The argument supplies no evidence that those links are part of an Ecosia claim flow or that viewers are promised anything for themselves.

citations.quote: Disclaimer: Some of the links in this description are Amazon affiliate links.
If your desired search engine isn't in the list of available search engines,, scroll down to One-Click Search Engines and select Find More Search Engines at the bottom.

opening.argument: The presentation begins as a general Firefox tutorial, but its worked example has a promotional arc. After explaining that viewers can choose among search engines, the presenter singles out Ecosia by its tree-planting benefit, installs its plug-in, makes it the default, and tests a search. That is more than mentioning an option: it demonstrates the full path from an appealing claim to repeated use. The tutorial's practical accuracy can make that invitation more persuasive, not less.

citations.quote: You could change it to Google, DuckDuckGo if you're into privacy, also different web sites as well.
So I'm gonna add Ecosia, which is a search engine that plants trees every time you use the search engine
Once you select the search engine, you're done. You don't have to save anything, it automatically saves, and when I do a search, it'll be at my new desired search engine.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The defense's account of a valid Firefox workflow does not answer why this example is framed around a benefit from using the chosen engine. The presenter does not merely name Ecosia alongside other options; he gives its tree-planting reason, adds it, and searches with it. That makes the instructional material a vehicle for encouraging use, even though the steps themselves are real.

citations.quote: Ecosia, which is a search engine that plants trees every time you use the search engine, so I'm going to select the search plug-in and then just select Add to Firefox
when I do a search, it'll be at my new desired search engine

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Using one engine as an example does not turn a browser tutorial into a scam. The presenter explains how to find a viewer's desired search engine, add it if necessary, select it as the default, and verify that the change worked. The argument identifies promotion but no deceptive promise or viewer reward.

citations.quote: If your desired search engine isn't in the list of available search engines,, scroll down to One-Click Search Engines and select Find More Search Engines at the bottom.
Test this to be sure that it worked properly by searching for something to see if it opens in the correct search engine.
